services.description:
Getting financed shouldn't be the stressful part of buying your next RV or powersports unit. Our finance team works with a network of lenders to find competitive rates and terms for every credit situation -- whether your credit is excellent, you're rebuilding, or you're financing your first big purchase. We do the shopping so you don't have to.

The smart move is to get pre-qualified before you start shopping. It takes just a few minutes, it tells you exactly what you can comfortably afford, and it lets you negotiate from a position of strength when you find the unit you love. There's no obligation, and it doesn't tie you to any particular unit.

We also help you protect your investment. Ask us about GAP coverage, which protects you if your unit is totaled or stolen and you owe more than it's worth, and extended service contracts that cover repairs after the factory warranty runs out. RVs and powersports units have a lot of systems, and these protections can save you from a big surprise bill down the road. We'll explain every option in plain language so you can decide what makes sense for you.

faq.question: Can I get financed if my credit isn't great?
faq.answer: Often, yes. We work with multiple lenders, including some who specialize in helping buyers with limited or rebuilding credit. Your rate and terms will reflect your credit situation, but we'll work hard to find you an option that fits your budget. faq.question: Does getting pre-qualified obligate me to buy?
faq.answer: Not at all. Pre-qualification just tells you what you can afford and what your rate might look like. It takes a few minutes, comes with no obligation, and isn't tied to any specific unit. It simply puts you in a stronger position when you do find the RV or powersports unit you want.

faq.question: What's the difference between GAP coverage and an extended service contract?
faq.answer: GAP coverage protects you financially if your unit is totaled or stolen and you owe more on the loan than the unit is worth -- it covers that 'gap.' An extended service contract covers the cost of mechanical repairs after your factory warranty expires. They solve two different problems, and we'll help you decide whether one or both makes sense for your situation.
